A chieftain of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, Aisha Yesufu, has warned that members of the party will no longer tolerate attacks on them, declaring that anyone who attacks them will be met with “equal force” as political tensions rise ahead of the 2027 general elections. Yesufu made the declaration during an interview on Channels Television’s Sunday Politics, days after suspected political thugs disrupted the party’s town hall meeting for its presidential candidate, Peter Obi, in Oregun, Lagos State. “I am prepared for war because I want peace. And they are coming out protecting… to try to defend myself, right to defend my life. It’s a fundamental right, it’s a human right, it’s a natural right, and I will protect myself,” she said. She accused President Bola Tinubu and members of the All Progressives Congress of failing to speak out against previous attacks on opposition supporters, while questioning why the President had condemned the recent incident involving the NDC. Recalling attacks and threats allegedly made against opposition supporters in different parts of the country, Yesufu cited the killing of an NDC supporter in Enugu, whom she said was the only son of his mother. According to her, the President’s position that all was fair in politics had emboldened political violence, adding that opposition supporters had previously chosen not to retaliate because they wanted to maintain peace. “The fact that some people think they have the monopoly of violence and they will unleash their thugs and their thugs will kill, they will maim, they will destroy, and they will not say anything, it has passed. We will no longer accept that,” she said. The NDC chieftain, however, denied threatening to initiate violence, insisting that her comments were about defending herself and other party members against attacks. 2027: Anambra women unveil door-to-door campaign for Tinubu 2027: Abiodun’s aides mobilise for Tinubu, Yayi, others Kwankwaso’s convoy attacked in Kano – Obi “I am not threatening violence, but anybody that comes to attack us will be met with force, equal force. I am not threatening violence. I am threatening that I am going to defend my life,” she added. The comments followed the November 12 attack on the NDC’s town hall meeting at Classique Event Centre in Oregun, Ikeja, where suspected political thugs reportedly disrupted preparations for the gathering involving Obi, his running mate, Rabiu Kwankwaso, and the party’s Lagos governorship candidate, Funso Doherty. Several attendees were injured during the incident, while vehicles were damaged and some journalists reportedly lost equipment. The meeting was later held after Obi arrived at the venue. The Lagos State chapter of the APC and the party’s presidential campaign council denied involvement in the attack and called for the perpetrators to be arrested. Tinubu also condemned violence at political events and directed security agencies to tackle political thuggery, stressing that all candidates and political parties should be allowed to campaign without intimidation. Speaking on the 2027 elections, Yesufu said the NDC was more confident of its chances than it was during the 2023 general election, adding that its members would not be intimidated. “I will tell you something, this 2027 election, we have more hope than we even did in that 2023, and we will continue to go on that. We are peace-loving people, but we are also people that are not going to take nonsense from anybody,” she said. She added that the party’s major concern was ensuring that its votes were protected and that its victory, if secured, was not overturned through electoral malpractice. “Winning is not our problem. The main issue is ensuring that when we win, nobody, born of man or woman, will rig our election,” Yesufu said. Christabel Ndoeche
